first_hunter_context.bar: Revenue $0.4M for Q3 2026 and EPS -$0.00 from a single sponsored estimate (Zacks SCR, 2026-09-01, https://s27.q4cdn.com/906368049/files/News/2026/Zacks_SCR_Research_09012026_BLRX_Vandermosten.pdf). No second estimate source was found. The company guide is cash runway 'into the first half of 2027' (Q2 release 2026-08-31, https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/biolinerx-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update-302864836.html). Revenue is royalty only: Q2 was $294K on $1.6M of APHEXDA sales, and Q2 2025 was $304K. That makes $0.4M look high, but the stock does not trade on this line. The bar has one source, so every finding is capped small.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: No usable option chain (baseline: empty_chain), so there is no skew. Short interest about 145.6K ADS, about 2.9% of float, 8.9-11.1 days to cover, from late-October trackers (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=BLRX, https://equibles.com/stocks/blrx/short-interest). The trend is flat to falling, and a June borrow fee of 39.3% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/blrx/). Not a crowded short. Liquidity is extreme: 20-day average volume 26.6K ADS, about $26K a day at $0.99. Armistice Capital holds the August 2026 offering ADSs and 2.02M warrants struck at $2.78, and an F-1 resale registration was filed 2026-09-25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001498403/000117891326004612/zk2636130.htm). The stock is at its 52-week low, -51.5% over 20 days and -23.9% over 5. Market cap is about $7M on roughly 7.0M ADS (derived from the F-1 ownership table at 600 ordinary shares per ADS).

evidence.text: The Q3 release is the first scheduled update of the cash runway since the Nov 18 royalty sale. BioLineRx sells its 14.4% APHEXDA royalty to Soleus for $5.6M, about 6x the roughly $0.9M a year that royalty yields at Q2's $1.6M a quarter of sales. Part of the money goes to a partial repayment of the BlackRock loan, which removes a $4M minimum-cash covenant. The Nov 18 release stated no new runway. The standing guide is 'into 1H 2027', set on $13.1M of cash at June 30. My estimate is about $11-12M at Sept 30 (13.1 + 3.3 net August raise - ~$3.5M quarterly burn - ~$1.1M loan amortisation), against a market cap of about $7M. A runway extended to 2H 2027 or beyond, plus net cash near the market cap, is the likely new content.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior prints, closes from Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BLRX?range=1y&interval=1d): Q3'25 on 2025-11-24 +7.7%; FY25 on 2026-03-23 -12.5%; Q1'26 on 2026-05-27 +6.6% (first GLIX1 patient); Q2'26 on 2026-08-31 +7.7%, the day after an offering-led drop. Runway was 'maintained' at each print, never extended. The royalty-sale day itself (2026-11-18) closed +2.7% on 295K volume, then gave it back (-8% over 2 sessions).
evidence.why_not_priced: The deal release gave no cash balance and no runway. The stock fell from $1.15 to $0.99 after it, so the market has not bid it up on the extension. A market that had priced a longer runway would not hold the ADS near net cash. The counterweight is that the slide is a seller (finding 2), not a reading of the balance sheet.
evidence.independence: Q2 release (cash $13.1M, runway into 1H27, $6.7M loan): https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/biolinerx-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update-302864836.html. Zacks 1H26 burn $5.5M: https://s27.q4cdn.com/906368049/files/News/2026/Zacks_SCR_Research_09012026_BLRX_Vandermosten.pdf. The extension itself is my inference and is not company-stated.

evidence.text: A steady, news-free decline into the print: closes went from $2.04 (Oct 23) to $0.99 (Nov 20), down on almost every session, with volume rising from 2-5K to 10-33K ADS a day. The only company news in the period was positive or neutral (SNO posters with no significant adverse events, 4th GLIX1 cohort dosing, the royalty sale). The likely seller is the August offering investor. Armistice holds ADSs from the $2.78 offering and had an F-1 resale registration filed 2026-09-25, and $2.78 warrants that are deep out of the money. Tax-loss selling in a name -74% from its high fits too. If that seller is not finished, it sells into whatever the print says.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August raise drew -5.8% on announcement (2.76 to 2.60) and a 20% drop reported in late August coverage. The royalty-sale day saw a +2.7% close quickly sold back down.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is the price itself. The question is only whether the selling continues through Monday. A finished seller would show as volume drying up with the price stabilising; instead Nov 19 traded 32K ADS at -7.8%. Nov 20 was lighter (7.5K, intraday).
evidence.independence: Armistice's holding and resale registration: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001498403/000117891326004612/zk2636130.htm. Offering terms: https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/biolinerx-announces-3-75-million-registered-direct-offering-and-concurrent-private-placement-302862746.html. No document shows Armistice actually selling, so the cause is an inference.

evidence.text: The motixafortide PDAC trial (CheMo4METPANC, NCT04543071) changed to 'Active, not recruiting' in its 2026-09-16 registry update, against the 'enrolling' wording in the company's Q2 release. The company has guided the prespecified interim/futility analysis (at 40% of PFS events) to happen 'in 2026'. So the Q3 release has to either report on it, reaffirm the 2026 timing or slip it to 2027. The market cap of about $7M is near net cash and puts almost no value on PDAC (Zacks models a 20% probability). A disclosed pass would be a large positive; a slip or futility would be a small negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No PDAC readout since the ASCO 2025 pilot data (4 of 11 progression-free for more than a year); its reaction is not in my sources. The 2026 guide was reaffirmed in March and August without a measurable move attributable to it.
evidence.why_not_priced: The registry status change was not in any company release or in the coverage found. A market expecting a near-term interim on a $7M company would show some option value; the stock instead trades at about net cash. The status may only mean an enrolment pause or completion, not that a readout is imminent, so the size is small and centred near zero.
evidence.independence: Company guide 'interim/futility analysis ... anticipate will occur in 2026' in the Q2 release: https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/biolinerx-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update-302864836.html. The same guide appears in the FY25 release: https://biolinerx.gcs-web.com/node/14251.

evidence.text: Royalty revenue, the only reported revenue line, looks set to miss the single sponsored estimate: Zacks has Q3 revenue at $0.4M, while Q2 was $294K on $1.6M of APHEXDA sales (down from $1.7M a year earlier). Ayrmid, a private company, has published no sales figures since. The line is now largely sold to Soleus, so it carries little weight.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 revenue of $0.29M against $0.50M consensus (per Earnings Whispers) was followed by +7.7% on the print day, so the line has not moved the stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: The line is too small to price: about $0.3M against a $7M market cap.
evidence.independence: Q2 release figures: https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/biolinerx-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update-302864836.html. This shares a source with the bar.

evidence.text: The ADS closed below $1.00 on 2026-11-20 (intraday $0.99). A Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency notice needs 30 consecutive business days below $1, so the earliest is about January 2027. The company has handled this before with ADS ratio changes (to 1:600 on 2025-01-30, per the F-1).
The Soleus royalty sale closes on or about 2026-11-30 and needs Ayrmid's consent to direct remittance. Until it closes, the $5.6M is not cash.

GLIX1 Phase 1/2a: 4th of 5 cohorts dosing, no significant treatment-emergent adverse events, full dose-escalation results guided to 1H 2027. The registry was updated 2026-11-04 with 4 sites and primary completion June 2027.
Earnings Whispers' Q2 'loss of $0.77 per share vs breakeven consensus' as a bar for Q3 EPS
BiopharmaWatch 'typical move 6.8% over 3 past catalysts' as a base rate
A cause for the Oct 23 to Nov 20 slide in news or filings: none found beyond the Armistice resale F-1 and the royalty sale (searches on BLRX October/November 2026 news)
A 2026 Nasdaq deficiency notice (bid price or stockholders' equity): none found
APHEXDA sales disclosures from Ayrmid / Gamida Cell for 2026: none (Ayrmid is private; only real-world-data releases)
CheMo4METPANC interim/futility results: none published
Analyst commentary on the royalty sale: none found
A second consensus source for Q3: only Zacks SCR (sponsored); Earnings Whispers reported Q2 only
Company IR news page (ir.biolinerx.com/news-releases): HTTP 403; used PR Newswire and the Finviz sidebar instead

first_hunter_context.bar: Company Q3 2026 guide: revenue $7.7-7.8m, adj. EBITDA $(1.3)-$(1.2)m, given 2026-08-17 (https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/freightos-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-302852762.html). Street revenue consensus $7.83m per Finviz/MarketBeat in August (https://finviz.com/news/382895/freightos-shares-surge-14-as-q2-loss-beats-expectations) and $7.903m / EPS -$0.05 per a Chartmill snippet (page 403, undated). The consensus sits at or above the top of the guide. Two analysts (Craig-Hallum's George Sutton on the call; Freedom Broker, PT $2.50).
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is tiny. Massive.com: 36.2k shares short, ~1.0 days to cover as of 2026-09-30. Equibles: ~51.4k shares short, 0.1% short interest, 1.0 DTC as of 2026-10-05 (https://equibles.com/stocks/crgo/shortinterest; https://massive.com/quote/crgo). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. No options market, so there is no skew. Tape: spot $0.80, -75.6% from the 52w high, +33.7% off the 52w low ($0.58, early November), +8.3% over 20d, 20d realised vol 74.5%, ~86k shares/day (~$70k/day). Market cap ~$41.7m on 52.07m shares (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/CRGO/).

evidence.text: Q3 KPIs, pre-released 2026-10-15: GBV $437m (+30% YoY) against a company guide of $390-397m, ~11% above the top of the range; transactions 494k (+15%) against 481-490k. Platform revenue (Q2 $2.9m, +19%; Q3 2025 $2.6m) therefore likely prints ~$3.0-3.1m, at or above what the $7.7-7.8m revenue guide embedded. The release adds that 'GBV also reflected elevated freight rates', so part of the GBV beat is price, not take.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same setup twice. Q2 2026: KPI beat pre-released, revenue $7.7m beat the $7.2-7.4m guide, shares +14% pre-market (https://finviz.com/news/382895/freightos-shares-surge-14-as-q2-loss-beats-expectations). Q3 2025: KPI beat pre-released, revenue lagged estimates, stock -13.9% on the day (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CRGO/freightos-reports-third-quarter-2025-y3crjr4vg07w.html). The KPI beat alone has not decided the sign.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the KPIs have been public for five weeks, the stock has since fallen below $1 (Nasdaq notice) and rebounded to $0.80. What is not public is the translation into Platform revenue. If the market had fully priced a Platform beat, the stock would not sit at a ~0.7x EV/sales low.
evidence.independence: Q2 2026 precedent: the KPI beat translated into a revenue beat (https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/freightos-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-302852762.html). Same company, different quarter.

evidence.text: Solutions (software/data, ~62% of revenue: $19.6m of $29.5m in FY2025) is the swing line and looks soft. It was $4.8m in Q1 and $4.8m in Q2 2026 (Q2 -4% YoY, 'SaaS performance weaker than expected', 'renewal pricing pressure', insufficient new bookings), against a Q3 2025 comp of $5.1m, so a flat sequential print is ~-6% YoY. The Oct-15 KPI release also changed its wording: from July's 'Solutions progress will be discussed in the upcoming earnings release' to 'Solutions, which account for the majority of Freightos' revenue, are less directly reflected in these metrics. The Company will provide an update on Solutions performance'. That reads as a hedge. Net of Platform at ~$3.0-3.1m, total revenue reaches the $7.83-7.90m consensus only if Solutions is >= ~$4.8m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: revenue lagged estimates while KPIs beat, stock -13.9%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-23): -30%, conflated with the founder's board exit (https://www.freightwaves.com/news/freightos-stock-plummets-after-founder-resigns). Q2 2026: Solutions -4% was offset by a Platform/Clearit beat, +14%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street consensus ($7.83m Aug; $7.90m on Chartmill) sits at or above the top of the $7.7-7.8m guide. That implies Solutions is modelled at or above the Q2 level despite the Q3 2025 comp and the hedge. If the market had priced a Solutions decline, consensus would sit at or below the guide midpoint.
evidence.independence: Q2 call (TradingKey transcript, 2026-08-17): Solutions down on renewal pricing pressure, pipeline +30% QoQ, conversion 'to begin improving in H2' (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262112964-tradingkey). Q3 2025 Solutions $5.1m from https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CRGO/freightos-reports-third-quarter-2025-y3crjr4vg07w.html. Inference from wording plus a comp; no direct Solutions data point.

evidence.text: The freight-rate backdrop since the guide was set is stronger, which supports a Q4/FY GBV raise. The guide 'assumes freight price levels and market volumes as of August 2026'. WorldACD global air rates were $3.45/kg in week 45 (2-8 Nov 2026), +31% YoY; late-October spot was reported +38% YoY. Tonnage was flat to down. Platform revenue tracks transactions more than rates (Q3 2025: GBV +54%, Platform +15%), so the transmission to revenue is weak.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The Q2 2026 call kept FY GBV +19-21% after a Q2 GBV beat, and the stock rose +14% on the revenue/EBITDA beat, not on GBV.
evidence.why_not_priced: A sub-$1 microcap with two analysts and ~$70k/day of turnover; no one re-cuts a GBV guide from WorldACD. If priced, the stock would have rallied with the rate data rather than hitting a 52w low in early November.
evidence.independence: Company's own Oct-15 release: 'GBV also reflected elevated freight rates amid tight capacity and higher fuel costs' (https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/freightos-reports-platform-kpis-for-third-quarter-exceeding-management-expectations-302909936.html). Macro proxy; no direct confirmation of Q4 bookings.

evidence.text: Q4 2026 is the guided EBITDA-breakeven quarter. Guide: Q4 adj. EBITDA loss under $1m, crossing breakeven 'at some point during Q4', with the full impact of the March cost actions landing in Q4. Q2 liquidity was $21.4m (cash $13.3m plus $8.1m deposit) with burn tracking adj. EBITDA, and management said no financing is needed. Q3-end liquidity should therefore be ~$20m against a ~$41.7m market cap. A reaffirmation on the call lands on the guide and the cash path. The money question [sizing note removed] was answered: no raise is planned, so it is not a negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'lowest-ever adj. EBITDA loss' plus reiterated breakeven, +14% pre-market. FY2025 print (Feb 2026): breakeven reiterated, but the stock fell -30% on the founder's exit.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely public. What is unseen is whether Q3 EBITDA beats $(1.2)m and Q4 is reaffirmed. An EV of ~$22m on ~$30m of revenue says the market doubts the path; if it believed it, EV/sales would not sit near 0.7x.
evidence.independence: Q2 release figures (https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/freightos-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-302852762.html), which share the Q2 document with the transcript.

evidence.text: Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency notice dated 2026-11-10 (below $1 from 9 Sep to 9 Nov; cure by 2027-05-10). The company said it is weighing options 'including a possible reverse share split'. A reverse-split plan or an added AGM item could surface with results or on the call, which is typically a negative for a sub-$1 microcap.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent for this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The notice is public. Whether a split is announced in the window is uncertain, and the AGM proxy (filed Nov 4) shows no split item per FreightWaves' summary. If the market expected an imminent split, the stock would not have rallied +10% the day the notice came out.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: Proxy fight: founder Zvi Schreiber (~6%) seeks the removal of Chairman Udo Lange, annual director elections and a Platform-first strategy, and alleges the proxy card was 'rigged'. The vote is at the AGM on 2026-12-16; the board opposes all three proposals. The call may draw questions, but the vote resolves after the window.
Nasdaq bid-price cure deadline, 2027-05-10.
Mas (Latin American freighter airline) integration with Freightos eBooking/Pay
Next-gen 'Freightos for Forwarders' AI platform launch on 2026-11-10 (possible Solutions re-acceleration story on the call)
Chartmill Q3 consensus $7.903m revenue / -$0.05 EPS
ATM / F-3 shelf / new financing in 2026: none found beyond an older resale registration for holders; Q2 call said no financing needed
Short-interest build: none (0.1%, ~1 DTC)
A reliable Q1 2026 reaction (only spam domains) and a full 8-print reaction history (baseline empty, sec.gov 403)
Customer-level Solutions/SaaS churn signals (forums, reviews): nothing specific found; only management's 'renewal pricing pressure'
Counterparty news since Oct 15: mas airline integration (2026-10-20) and the Nov 10 AI forwarder platform launch; neither carries a revenue number
Ocean-rate data for November 2026: only fragments of undated Freightos weekly updates; air data used instead

The company gives no earnings guidance. Every finding is capped small because the bar is unsourced.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is about 140.0K units with about 2.0 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (41.9K at 09-15), per curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dlng/short-interest/). Equibles shows an identical 140,249 at 2026-05-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dlng/short-interest), so the figure is not fully reliable. Either way it is a few tenths of a percent of units: not crowded, and no squeeze mechanism. No skew: the baseline option chain is empty (status empty_chain). Tape: spot $2.95 on 2026-11-20, -11.1% over 20 days, -6.65% over 5 days, at the 52-week low and 31% off the high. Turnover is about 56K units a day (about $165K). The slide runs from 3.78 on Oct 1 to 2.95. It includes the Nov 13 ex-date of the $0.05 distribution (3.26 to 3.16) and the Nov 3 sanctions update (3.17 to 3.04 over two sessions), per Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DLNG?range=1y&interval=1d).

evidence.text: Q3 2026 is Clean Energy's first full quarter on its new Rio Grande LNG time charter (started 2026-04-30 at a higher rate that management called accretive). Q2 lost 20.5 off-hire days on that vessel between redeliveries and still printed voyage revenue $41.2M, adjusted EPU $0.39 and adjusted EBITDA $27.6M, with net interest costs down 26.9% YoY. Q3 should therefore show revenue around $42-43M and adjusted EPU at or above Q2's $0.39, against Q3 2025's $38.9M and $0.36. There is no consensus to beat, so the comparison is against the trailing quarters.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: From Yahoo daily bars, not the baseline, which is empty. Q2 2026 (bmo, 2026-09-08): net income +17% and revenue +6.7% YoY, stock 3.66 to 3.86, +5.5%. Q1 2026 (released 2026-05-29): adjusted net income -13% on lower Arctic Aurora hire and repairs, about -2%. Q4 2025 (released 2026-03-13): revenue and adjusted EBITDA down YoY, about -4% on the day and about -10% over two sessions, though the feed's dates appeared shifted by a day. Quarters with clean revenue have been bought; quarters with a softer revenue line have been sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: No published estimate exists, so nobody holds a number the full-quarter Rio Grande hire could beat or miss. The stock has fallen 22% since Oct 1 on sanctions headlines, not on operations. If the market had priced an improving quarter, the units would not sit at the 52-week low at roughly 2x annualised adjusted EPU.
evidence.independence: The Q4 2025 release (https://finviz.com/news/337229/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-reports-results-for-the-three-and-twelve-months-ended-december-31-2025) separately states that the Rio Grande charter is at a higher daily rate and expected to be accretive. It is the same company, a different document. Q2 2026 results also say drydockings fall in 2027-2028, not 2026 (https://quartr.com/events/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-dlng-q2-2026_FG0G6456). Contract coverage is 100% for 2026, so revenue is a utilisation question.

evidence.text: The release will restate the UK sanctions position. Regulations enacted 2026-05-20 bar UK persons from facilitating maritime transport of Russian-origin LNG from 2027-01-01 for the long-term Yamal Trade charters of the Yenisei River and Lena River (to 2033 and 2034; 34.5% of H1 2026 revenue). The company must replace UK-based providers, including insurers, and said on Nov 3 there is 'no assurance that replacement services will be available on comparable terms, or at all'. Losing the charters 'could cause a default under the debt agreements'. The results come six weeks before the deadline: any progress on replacement insurers would be new and positive; a repeat of the Nov 3 wording, or a charterer dispute, would be negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 3 sanctions update (released 16:05 ET) was followed by 3.17 to 3.04 over the next two sessions, about -4%. No earlier print carried a deadline this close.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock is at the 52-week low and fell after the Nov 3 update. What is not priced is the status of insurer replacement, which no public source reports for Dynagas: the search found no named replacement P&I club. If the market had priced a successful switch, the units would have recovered from the 52-week low. If it had priced a charter loss, they would trade well below a 2x multiple, since the two charters are 34.5% of revenue.
evidence.independence: Same jurisdictional fact in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/389607/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-reports-results-for-the-three-and-six-months-ended-june-30-2026), so the documents are not independent. Lloyd's lobbied for a delay to the UK insurance ban (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/uk/news/marine/lloyds-lobbies-for-delay-as-uks-ban-on-insuring-russian-lng-tankers-approaches-589518.aspx; date not verified). Shares the Nov 3 document with nothing else filed here.

evidence.text: The two other sanctions regimes eased after the Q2 print. On 2026-10-16 an Executive Order waived nearly all of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act's Russia provisions, including those that would have reached Novatek as Yamal LNG's controlling shareholder (Act signed 2026-09-18). The EU's 21st package (adopted 2026-07-23) exempts legacy pre-2022 long-term contracts to at least 2027-07-25, and the company believes the Yamal charters qualify. The UK rule is the remaining live constraint.

evidence.text: GAAP headline is likely to swing on the convertibles' fair-value line. VNET runs convertible notes (RMB4.84bn carrying value at 6-30) through 'changes in fair value of financial instruments': Q1 2026's net loss of RMB2.23bn came while the stock rose, and Q2 had a RMB47.1m fair-value loss. With the ADS down sharply over Q3, a fair-value gain is likely and a headline swing to GAAP profit is possible.
